- Karthik: can you confirm the reserve % you're comfortable committing to for DEAL-8721 if Orion hits MRR thresholds by July 14?
- Laura: what are the billing cadence constraints if we take a partial-month reserved commitment vs. burst credits?

High level items in the CSV: recent ACV uplift from Orion, expected pilot model load ~120k tokens/day at peak, potential Q3 uplift scenarios in the comments column.

Marissa, Laura, team —

Thanks Alex / Marissa —

I ran conservative and aggressive scenarios against the pipeline CSV. If Orion is committed to the July 14 ramp and we see N-week smoothing from their onboarding, my recommendation is:

- Conservative: 2 reserved slots for the first 2 weeks, plus 4 burst-capable instances.
- Aggressive: 4 reserved slots day-one, scale to 8 within 10 business days.

Key assumptions that change this: average sequence length (assumed 2.8k tokens), concurrency (assumed 6 concurrent requests at peak), and our quantization profile for the deployed variant.

Actionable asks:
1) Laura: which billing construct lets us (A) reserve fewer slots initially and (B) convert burst usage to reserved credit retroactively? I want to model the cashflow and revenue recognition impacts before we commit.
2) Ben / Logan: what are your real world lead times to spin up N=4 extra reserved slots (not burst) if we decide Wed? Are there region-specific constraints?

I'll surface a short table in the Wed notes mapping cost vs latency tradeoffs.

Karthik
Sr Manager, Capacity Planning

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Alex Perez <aperez@orionsys.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jul 2029 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Sprint-aligned GPU sourcing: week of Jul 8 - runway check

Folks —

Short answer on billing: we can support a prorated reserved commitment with a minimum of two billing cycles if we use our 'ramp clause' template. That lets us take a smaller reserve initially and convert burst consumption to reserved credit up to 30 days retrospectively, subject to finance sign-off.

I've attached a cost sensitivity workbook (cost_scenario_q3.xlsx) with three scenarios: prorated partial reserve, prorated + burst-to-reserve conversion, and upfront 3-month reserve. For DEAL-8721, the prorated partial-reserve shows the lowest cash outlay in month-1 while protecting margin after we scale.

Please review rows labeled "Decision Sensitivity" — they directly feed the sales approval packet. If we intend to go with prorated partial-reserve I need a headcount of internal discounts/credits requested (if any) and the legal counterparty for the contract.

Laura
Head of Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: cost_scenario_q3.xlsx

- Provide burst pool access up to 12 additional instances for the pilot window (billing to match the prorated model Laura outlined).
